title: How to Lead Even When You Don't Know Where You Are Going

canonicalEdition.name: First edition
canonicalEdition.sourceProvenance: Frozen web bundle only: bibliographic records, table-of-contents evidence, official publication metadata, and narrow secondary summary support. Paraphrase-first; no full text frozen.

anchorSummary: Horowitz treats uncertainty as a leadership environment, not an exception, and argues that the CEO's psychological discipline is what lets the organization keep moving when the future is still murky.
coreClaim: The leader's first job in uncertainty is to stay psychologically functional enough to create clarity and momentum for others without pretending certainty they do not possess.
distinctMechanism: Horowitz combines CEO psychology, communication, and directional leadership into one principle: the company takes cues from how the leader handles ambiguity, not from whether ambiguity disappears.
requiredAnchors: The most difficult CEO skill is psychological, because the role offers little training and constant pressure.
Leadership under uncertainty requires directional clarity without fake omniscience.
Followers read the leader's steadiness, communication, and standards when the route is still unresolved.
specificApplications: Use self-management to keep ambiguity from turning into organizational panic.
Communicate what is known, unknown, and next without posturing.
Lead with direction and standards even when the route is still unfolding.
commonMisreadings: Treating the chapter as license for bluffing certainty instead of leading honestly under ambiguity.
Reducing psychological management to positive thinking rather than disciplined emotional control.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard mode must show how a leader's unmanaged fear or confusion spreads through the company faster than any official message.
thresholdQuestion: What must a leader make clear when they cannot yet make everything certain?
